title: The Last Supper
summary: In The Last Supper, kids slow down long enough to see the choice, pressure, or promise inside the passage. Jesus gave His followers a meal to remember His saving death. Jesus shared the Last Supper and pointed His disciples to His sacrifice.

read_it.prompt: Read Luke 22:14-20 and underline the part that best shows Jesus.

tell_it: Jesus shared the Last Supper and pointed His disciples to His sacrifice. Jesus shared bread and cup with His disciples and told them to remember Him. The pressure in the scene helps the lesson feel real.
understand_it: Jesus gave His followers a meal to remember His saving death. The Last Supper gives children a way to connect the Bible event to choices they actually face.
age_5_7_explanation: Jesus shared the Last Supper and pointed His disciples to His sacrifice.
age_8_11_explanation: Jesus shared bread and cup with His disciples and told them to remember Him. Kids can practice retelling it with the beginning, hard moment, and God-centered ending.
teen_explanation: Jesus gave His followers a meal to remember His saving death. A teen discussion can press into why the story mattered then and how the same truth can reshape choices now.
key_truths: Jesus gave His followers a meal to remember His saving death.
The Last Supper shows Jesus through a real Bible moment, not a slogan.
When kids take communion or hear about it, this story helps them connect the meal to Jesus' love and rescue.
life_application: When kids take communion or hear about it, this story helps them connect the meal to Jesus' love and rescue.

quiz_questions.question: Which answer keeps The Last Supper connected to the actual passage?
choices: The disciples served the crowd leftovers
quiz_questions.explanation: Jesus is the story detail to remember. The bigger lesson grows out of that detail instead of floating away from the passage.

quiz_questions.question: Which response best fits the lesson's point?
choices: Pretend the hard part in The Last Supper is not hard.
Use The Last Supper only to win a trivia point.
Ignore what God shows in The Last Supper.

quiz_questions.answer: When kids take communion or hear about it, this story helps them connect the meal to Jesus' love and rescue.
quiz_questions.explanation: A useful Bible lesson changes how we see a real choice. Jesus gave His followers a meal to remember His saving death.

memory_verse.prompt: Luke 22:19 gives this lesson a short Scripture anchor to remember.

discussion_questions: Who needed help, courage, correction, or mercy in The Last Supper?
What truth should a kid remember after reading The Last Supper?
How can the group pray about The Last Supper without using pretend-perfect answers?

activity.title: Remembering Meal Symbols
activity.instructions: Draw bread and cup symbols, then write what Jesus told His friends to remember.

prayer_prompt: Lord, use The Last Supper to teach my heart, not just my memory. Help me take one faithful next step after reading The Last Supper.
